summary: Per-card playtesting: N lane-agents, each with its own browser, tests a bucket of cards by tutoring each into hand and playing it.

notPlayed.notes: Card definition file has no effects/abilities block (metadata only), so the engine never offers it — effectively unimplemented.
Not offered as playSpell even after playing a friendly unit — engine gates it on having enemy units at battlefields, which goldfish never provides. Force-executing the move was rejected silently.

playSpell correctly NOT offered on turn 1 (no unit at any battlefield to target). Could not construct a state with both a unit at a battlefield and ≥4 energy within the goldfish flow (turn-3 energy resets to 0). No defect observed in target-legality gating.

void-rush.ts sequence step 2 is {type:'banish', target:{type:'card'}} — playSpell's spellEffectHasLegalTargets gates on that generic card target at cast time and finds none, so the spell is never legal. Target should be scoped to the revealed cards (pending-value), not a board card
Could not get the spell to cast under any board state tried (no enemy, friendly unit, enemy unit at base). Goldfish AI never plays units.

confirmed.what: Damage state fields inconsistent
confirmed.expected: meta.damage should reflect the 2 damage marked on the unit so UI/death checks see it.
confirmed.observed: meta.damage=0 while meta.__counters.damage=2 on the same card in the state snapshot.
confirmed.reason: Two disjoint damage stores exist and only combat keeps them in sync. Core `addCounter` writes to `meta.__counters[type]` (operations-impl.ts:459), never to top-level `meta.damage`. Spell/ability damage (Monster Harpoon unl-014-219, Dancing Grenade unl-020-219) goes through effect-executor.ts:407 which only calls `ctx.counters.addCounter(targetId,"damage",amount)` — so `meta.__counters.damage=2` but `meta.damage` stays 0. The `assignDamage` (combat.ts:195) and `addDamage` (counters.ts:65) moves do the same. Only `resolveFullCombat` (combat.ts:381-392) writes both the counter AND `updateCardMeta({damage:…})`. Meanwhile all readers use the top-level field: end-of-turn clear at riftbound-flow.ts:503 checks `meta.damage>0`, and UI reads `card.meta?.damage` at renderer.js:688, overlays.js:94, combat.js:47 — so spell-dealt damage is invisible to UI and the end-step clear, exactly matching the observed `meta.damage=0` / `meta.__counters.damage=2` snapshot.

confirmed.what: Empower activated ability not available
confirmed.expected: activateAbility move offered for Sandspinner with cost [2] (5 base − 3 discount, since I control 2 runes ≤ 4) while I have 4 energy
confirmed.observed: No activateAbility entry for player-1-main-999-ven-001-166 in moves list; forcing executeMove('activateAbility',{abilityIndex:0,...}) was a no-op (energy unchanged, no state change, no error)
confirmed.reason: ven-001-166's Empower keyword ability never reaches the engine as an activated ability, so activateAbility is neither enumerated nor executable. Chain: ven.json:21-23 stores "abilities": [null] for ven-001-166 (generator parse miss on "[Empower] [5]. This ability costs [3] less…"). all-cards.ts:805-807 (adaptJsonCard) filters the null and leaves abilities undefined, so enrich-cards.ts:29 re-runs parseAbilities on rulesText. parser/index.ts has no handler for the "[Empower] <cost>" keyword-ability form (only parseEmpowerEffect at :2406 for the verb, disempower-cost at :3365, and empower-trigger at :3939), so the runtime parse yields only [{type:"static", effect:{keyword:"Deflect",…}}] — verified by executing getAllCards() with bun. server.ts:725/973 registers that abilities array verbatim into the global registry. In chain-moves.ts, collectActivatedAbilities:256 skips it (type !== "activated"), so the enumerator at :732-738 emits no activateAbility entry; and the condition at :570-574 (abilities[0].type !== "activated" → return false) makes a forced executeMove a silent no-op — matching the observed "no entry in moves list; forced call was no-op, no error". ven-054-166 (ven.json:1777 "abilities": []) hits the same path: runtime parseAbilities returns success:false, abilities stays undefined, getAbilities (card-lookup.ts:163) returns [], enumerator/condition see nothing.

confirmed.what: Trigger 'When you play your second card in a turn' fires on every card play
confirmed.expected: Ability should trigger exactly once, on the second card played in a turn
confirmed.observed: Ability went on the chain when Darius (1st card) was played, again on the 2nd card, and again on the 3rd card. Card def trigger is {event:'play-card', on:'self'} with no 'second card' condition.
confirmed.reason: Runtime ability for ogn-027-298 (from parser, not ogn.json) is trigger={event:"play-card", on:"controller", restrictions:[{count:2, type:"nth-time-each-turn"}]}. toTriggerableAbilities() at trigger-runner.ts:85-88 copies only {event, on} and drops `restrictions`; triggerMatchesEvent() at trigger-matcher.ts:132-136 matches on:"controller" whenever event.playerId === card.owner. No `nth-time-each-turn` handling exists anywhere in the engine (grep: zero hits). Result: the ability goes on the chain for every card the controller plays — 1st (Darius), 2nd, 3rd — instead of only the 2nd. (Report's cited `on:"self"` is from ogn.json, which is not loaded — JSON_SETS=[venJson] at all-cards.ts:828; the TS card def has no abilities so the parser output is used. The observed behavior is nonetheless correct.)

confirmed.what: No prompt for optional additional cost
confirmed.expected: playUnit should prompt 'You may kill a friendly gear as an additional cost' (a friendly gear was on the board)
confirmed.observed: No pendingChoice, no alternate move variant; unit went straight to base for 3 energy with the friendly gear untouched
confirmed.reason: zaun-punk.ts:4-16 defines the card with no `abilities` field — only static data + rulesText. The optional "kill a friendly gear as an additional cost" is not encoded as an ability (contrast pyke-dockside-butcher.ts:14-34 which at least encodes the paid-additional-cost payoff). Even if it were, playUnit at riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:378-547 has no additional-cost handling: the enumerator (461-514) only emits `{cardId, location: "base"}` with no cost-variant, and the reducer (515-546) just calls deductCost with `{}`, moves the card, exhausts it, and fires triggers — never sets a pendingChoice and never touches the friendly gear. So the observed behavior (unit goes straight to base for 3 energy, no prompt) is exactly what the code does.

confirmed.what: 'if you paid the additional cost' condition not checked
confirmed.expected: The 'kill a gear' trigger should only fire if the optional additional cost was paid
confirmed.observed: Additional cost was never offered/paid, yet the on-play trigger put {type:'kill', target:{type:'gear'}} on the chain and killed the friendly Orb of Regret (trash went 0→1)
confirmed.reason: The parser correctly emits condition {type:"paid-additional-cost"} on Zaun Punk's play-self trigger (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText). However, the trigger path's condition gate — evaluateTriggerCondition() at trigger-runner.ts:108-121 — only handles c.type === "legion" (line 117) and returns true for every other condition type (line 120, documented as "permissive"). So {type:"paid-additional-cost"} passes the filter at fireTriggers() line 266-268, the trigger is pushed onto the chain (line 297-312) with effect {type:"kill", target:{type:"gear"}}, and executeResolvedItem() (chain-moves.ts:98-179) executes it with no condition re-check. The correct evaluator for this condition type exists at static-abilities.ts:227-229 (checks ctx.draft.additionalCostsPaid?.[source.id]) but is never invoked on the trigger path. Additionally, the first sentence of the rules text produces no ability (parser output has only the triggered ability), so the optional additional cost is never offered — additionalCostsPaid stays unset — yet the kill still fires.

confirmed.what: On-play trigger does not fire
confirmed.expected: 'When you play me … you may ready something besides me that's exhausted' — with an exhausted Forecaster already at base, playing Jayce should put a triggered ability on the chain and prompt to ready a target
confirmed.observed: chain=null, pendingChoice=null after playing Jayce; the exhausted Forecaster stayed exhausted. Card def has abilities:[] and parseSuccess:false.
confirmed.reason: On-play trigger for ven-068a-166 (Jayce) does not fire. Root cause differs from the report's hypothesis: the JSON's abilities:[] / parseSuccess:false (ven.json:2127-2128) is NOT the cause — adaptJsonCard (all-cards.ts:807) maps the empty array to undefined, so enrichCard (enrich-cards.ts:22-31) re-parses rulesText at runtime and DOES attach a triggered ability. The parser emits trigger.event = "play-self-or-play-gear" (parser/index.ts:3986). When Jayce is played, the engine fires event type "play-self" (moves/cards.ts:533/669/1157), and triggerMatchesEvent does a strict equality check `trigger.event !== event.type` (trigger-matcher.ts:84) — "play-self-or-play-gear" ≠ "play-self", so it returns false. The compound event "play-self-or-play-gear" is not mapped or decomposed anywhere in the engine (grep: zero hits outside the parser). Result: findMatchingTriggers returns no matches, fireTriggers returns 0 without adding to the chain (trigger-runner.ts:287-289), yielding the observed chain=null, pendingChoice=null and the exhausted Forecaster staying exhausted.

confirmed.what: Energy cost reduction not applied
confirmed.expected: With a 2-might unit controlled, Sky Splitter should cost 8-2=6 energy
confirmed.observed: Energy went 12→4 on cast (full 8 paid). Card def's static cost-reduction ability has effects:[] (description-only stub).
confirmed.reason: Sky Splitter's cost-reduction is a description-only stub. In ogn.json:463-470 the static ability is `{type:"static", effect:{type:"sequence", effects:[], description:"..."}}` — no `cost-reduction` effect node. The TS def (sky-splitter.ts:4-16) has no `abilities` field and no `interactiveCostReduction`. The engine's deductCost (game-definition/moves/cards.ts:260-267) only subtracts `meta.costModifier` and `getInteractiveReduction` (requires `interactiveCostReduction:"target-might"`, card-lookup.ts:207-208); it never scans the played card's own statics, and `computeStaticCostReduction` (operations/static-cost-reduction.ts) has no non-test callers and explicitly skips the played card / `target:"self"` anyway. Result: full printed 8 energy is deducted → 12→4, not 12→6.

confirmed.what: 'Deal 5 to a unit at a battlefield' does not apply damage
confirmed.expected: Target unit (Lecturing Yordle, 2 might) should take 5 damage and die
confirmed.observed: After both players passed and chain cleared, target still at battlefield with meta.damage=0; only the spell itself moved to trash. Game log shows 'dev cast Sky Splitter' then priority passes, no damage/death entry.
confirmed.reason: Sky Splitter's parsed effect ({type:"damage", amount:5, target:{type:"unit",location:"battlefield"}}) reaches executeEffect via chain resolution, but the "damage" case at effect-executor.ts:407 applies damage via `ctx.counters.addCounter(targetId, "damage", amount)`. The real core impl (core/src/operations/operations-impl.ts:450-459) writes that to `cardMetas[id].__counters.damage`, not the top-level `meta.damage` field. State-based death checks (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:94) and the server/UI read `meta.damage` (initialized to 0 at server.ts:711), so the write is invisible: meta.damage stays 0 and the unit never dies. Unit tests pass only because they mock addCounter to write straight to meta[counter] (wave5-cost-primitives.test.ts:104-109), masking the mismatch. Affects all executeEffect "damage" effects, including ogn-014-298.

confirmed.what: Crumbling Sands offered as playSpell with no target and no spell on the chain; playing it puts {type:'counter'} on chain with no target and it resolves doing nothing
confirmed.expected: 'Counter a spell' requires a spell on the chain as a target; should not be enumerated as a legal move when the chain is empty (and the 'if an opponent has played another spell this turn' condition is also unmet)
confirmed.observed: playSpell listed with no targets param on an empty board/chain; energy 5→4; chain item {effect:{type:'counter'}} with no targets; resolved to nothing
confirmed.reason: Parser output for ven-039-166 rulesText is `{type:"spell", timing:"reaction", effect:{type:"counter"}}` — no `target` descriptor and no condition (parser/index.ts:1777-1781 matches "Counter a spell if an opponent has played another spell this turn." via `/^Counter (a spell.*...)\.?$/i` and returns bare `{type:"counter"}`, dropping both the spell-on-chain target and the opponent-played-another-spell condition). In the engine, `spellEffectHasLegalTargets` (cards.ts:303-328) returns `true` for any effect lacking `target`/`target1`/`target2`, so the playSpell condition (cards.ts:759) and enumerator gate (cards.ts:840) both pass on an empty chain; the enumerator then falls into the non-card-target branch (cards.ts:848-873) and emits `{playerId, cardId}` with no `targets`. The reducer puts `{effect:{type:"counter"}, targets:undefined}` on the chain (cards.ts:918-925) after deducting cost. On resolution, `case "counter"` (effect-executor.ts:818-835) checks `chain.items.length > 0` and silently no-ops when nothing is below it. Net: Crumbling Sands is offered and playable with no target on an empty chain, spends 1 energy, and resolves doing nothing.

confirmed.what: 'Spend 2 XP: [Buff] me' activated ability is offered and activates with 0 XP on the card
confirmed.expected: activateAbility should be gated on having ≥2 XP counters; activating should remove 2 XP
confirmed.observed: Freshly played (0 XP), activateAbility{abilityIndex:3} was in moves; executing it put a buff effect on the chain with no XP consumed
confirmed.reason: Runtime parse of unl-102-219 yields ability index 3 = {type:"activated", cost:{xp:2}, effect:{type:"buff",target:"self"}} (verified via getAllCards()). The activateAbility move never inspects cost.xp: condition checks only cost.energy/power/exhaust/kill (chain-moves.ts:602-674, esp. 609/621/638/657); enumerator likewise (chain-moves.ts:749-824); reducer's deductAbilityCost handles only energy/power (chain-moves.ts:370-418) and inline handles only exhaust/kill (chain-moves.ts:865-886). Engine repro with player.xp=0: checkMoveLegal→true, enumerateMoves offers {abilityIndex:3}, applyMove succeeds, buff item lands on chain, player.xp stays 0.

confirmed.what: On-play trigger 'play a 1 Might Recruit unit token at your base' resolves but no token is created
confirmed.expected: After the create-token chain item resolves, a Recruit unit token (might 1) should be in base zone
confirmed.observed: Chain item {type:'create-token', token:{name:'Recruit',might:1}, location:'base'} resolved; base afterward contains only the gear itself, no token
confirmed.reason: buildEffectContext (chain-moves.ts:43-92) constructs the EffectContext used to resolve chain items but never sets `createCardInZone` on the returned object (see the return at lines 78-91 — only cards/counters/draft/fireTriggers/playerId/sourceCardId/sourceZone/zones are set). When ogn-212-298's play-self trigger places {type:'create-token', token:{name:'Recruit',might:1}, location:'base'} on the chain and it later resolves via executeResolvedItem→buildEffectContext→executeEffect, effect-executor.ts:837-840 hits `if (!ctx.createCardInZone) { break; }` and silently skips token creation. The core zones API does expose createCardInZone (used directly in moves/token.ts:114-151), but buildEffectContext neither accepts it in its context param type (lines 47-70) nor wires it into the EffectContext, so any create-token effect resolved off the chain is a no-op.

confirmed.what: 'Kill this: Recycle up to 4 cards from trashes' activated ability is never offered
confirmed.expected: activateAbility for the gear should appear in moves once it's in play (‘up to 4’ includes 0, so empty trashes shouldn't gate it)
confirmed.observed: No activateAbility entry for player-1-main-999-ogn-212-298 in moves after the gear resolved to base
confirmed.reason: Forge of the Future (ogn-212-298) defines its activated ability with cost `{ kill: "self" }` (forge-of-the-future.ts:26). The activateAbility enumerator (chain-moves.ts:808-824) and condition (chain-moves.ts:657-673) handle kill costs by calling resolveTarget(cost.kill, …) — which for "self" returns [hostCardId] (target-resolver.ts:75) — and then unconditionally filtering out the host card via `.filter((id) => id !== entry.hostCardId)` (line 820) / `.filter((id) => id !== cardId)` (line 666). The result is an empty options list, so the enumerator hits `continue` at line 822 and the condition returns false at line 668. The self-exclusion was written for Malzahar-style "kill another friendly permanent" costs (comment at line 656) but incorrectly also blocks `kill: "self"`, so the ability is never offered in moves regardless of trash contents.

confirmed.what: 'When you choose or ready me, give me +1 Might this turn' does not fire when Irelia readies during Awaken
confirmed.expected: After turn cycles and Irelia readies at start of controller's turn, might should be 5 (base 4 +1) for that turn
confirmed.observed: Turn 1: played exhausted, might 4. Turn 3 (after auto-cycle): exhausted=false, might still 4; no chain item, no pendingChoice
confirmed.reason: Awaken phase readies cards without firing any trigger. riftbound-flow.ts:182-218 (awaken.onBegin) calls context.cards.updateCardMeta(cardId, {exhausted: false}) but never calls fireTriggers; the readyAll move (turn.ts:188-205) likewise only sets the flag. There is no "ready" variant in GameEvent (abilities/game-events.ts:11-35) and no "ready" entry in EVENT_MAP (abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:48-73), even though TriggerEvent in riftbound-types (trigger-types.ts:52) declares "ready". So a "when you ready me" trigger can never match. Compounding: ven.json:4575-4578 stores abilities:[null,null] for ven-174-166, so the card has no structured ability to fire even if the event existed. Net effect matches the observation: after auto-cycle, exhausted=false, might stays 4, no chain item.

confirmed.what: Morbid Return is never enumerated as a legal playSpell even with a unit in the controller's trash
confirmed.expected: With Watchful Sentry (unit) in player-1 trash and 28 energy, playSpell for ogn-170-298 should appear (with a target prompt for the trash unit)
confirmed.observed: trash count=2 (incl. a unit), card in hand, energy 28; moves list contains zero playSpell entries for ogn-170-298; force-executing playSpell returns 400
confirmed.reason: Repro (bun script driving the real playSpell condition/enumerator with the actual enriched def for ogn-170-298): with a unit in P1's trash and no board units, condition=false and enumerator=[]; with a board unit present, it wrongly enumerates the board unit as the target and never the trash unit. Root cause: the parser gives Morbid Return effect.target={type:"unit",location:"trash"}, but resolveTarget() sources candidates only from getBoardCardIds (base + battlefield zones) at target-resolver.ts:89/166-191, and the location filter chain at target-resolver.ts:125-141 handles only "here"/"base"/"battlefield*" — there is no "trash" branch. So targetDescriptorIsSatisfiable (cards.ts:357-366) resolves against board units, returning [] on an empty board, which makes spellEffectHasLegalTargets false and blocks both the condition (cards.ts:758-773) and the enumerator (cards.ts:840-842). Force-executing hits the same condition path → 400.

confirmed.what: 'When you choose a friendly unit, you may pay [1] and exhaust this to draw 1' does not trigger when a friendly unit is chosen by a spell
confirmed.expected: After Stupefy resolves targeting friendly Keeper of Masks, a pendingChoice/chain item should offer paying 1 + exhausting Spirit Wheel to draw 1
confirmed.observed: Stupefy resolved on the friendly unit (might 2→1); no pendingChoice, no chain item referencing sfd-144-221, Spirit Wheel remained exhausted=false, hand size unchanged by the trigger
confirmed.reason: The engine never emits a `choose` GameEvent, so Spirit Wheel's trigger `{event:"choose", on:{cardType:"unit",controller:"friendly"}}` (spirit-wheel.ts:23-26) can never match. The event type is defined (game-events.ts:33) and mapped (trigger-matcher.ts:53), but a repo-wide grep shows zero `fireTriggers({...type:"choose"...})` call sites in production code — the only construction is in a unit test (engine-gaps-phase2.test.ts:315). When Stupefy is played, the target is bound at cards.ts:861-867 and the spell is placed on the chain at cards.ts:921-925 with no `choose` event fired; resolution at chain-moves.ts:179-204 fires only `play-spell`/`play-card`; and the `choose-target` pending-choice reducer (pending-choice.ts:160-172) also fires nothing. Secondary defect: even if emitted, the event shape `{cardId, chooserId}` lacks `owner`/`playerId`, so trigger-matcher.ts:153 yields `subjectOwner=undefined` and line 178 rejects the match for `controller:"friendly"`.

confirmed.what: Static '+1 Might while you have another unit here' not applied
confirmed.expected: With Forecaster also at base, Trusty Ramhound should show might 3 (base 2 +1)
confirmed.observed: Both units at base; state reports Ramhound might=2 (state does reflect effective might — Stupefy debuff earlier showed 2→1 on another unit)
confirmed.reason: trusty-ramhound.ts:4-15 defines no `abilities` array (only `rulesText`), so `registry.getAbilities()` (card-lookup.ts:162-163) returns [] and `recalculateStaticEffects` (static-abilities.ts:483) never applies the +1 might modifier. Other sfd cards (e.g. loyal-pup.ts:27) do carry an `abilities` field, confirming this is the wiring path. Secondary gap: even if wired, `evaluateCondition` has no "another unit here" condition — the closest, `while-alone` (static-abilities.ts:156-165), returns false outside battlefields, so it wouldn't work at base either.

confirmed.what: Dealing 6 damage to a 3-might unit does not kill it
confirmed.expected: Per rule 143.2.a, Vanguard Captain (might 3) should be killed and moved to trash after taking 6 damage
confirmed.observed: Spell resolved (energy 9→4, spell to trash), but Vanguard Captain remained on battlefield-player-1-bf with might 3; trash only incremented by 1 (the spell)
confirmed.reason: Falling Comet (ogn-085-298) has no `abilities` array — only display-only `rulesText` (falling-comet.ts:4-15). The playSpell reducer looks up the effect via `registry.getAbilities(cardId).find(a => a.type === "spell")?.effect` (cards.ts:892-894) and stores it on the chain item; for this card that is `undefined`. On resolution, `executeResolvedItem` sees `rawEffect === undefined`, retries the same registry lookup, again gets no spell ability, and returns without ever calling `executeEffect` (chain-moves.ts:108-123). Thus no `damage` effect runs, `performCleanup`'s rule-520 check (state-based-checks.ts:92-173) sees `meta.damage === 0`, and Vanguard Captain (might 3) is never killed. Cost deduction (cards.ts:883, energy 9→4) and moving the spell to trash happen unconditionally, matching the observed state. Contrast bullet-time.ts which correctly declares `abilities: [{ type: "spell", effect: { type: "damage", … } }]`. Defect is a missing card ability definition (riftbound-cards layer), not the death-check logic itself.

confirmed.what: Lethal damage does not kill the target
confirmed.expected: Per rule 143.2.a, a unit with damage ≥ might is killed. Watchful Sentry (might 1) taking 2 damage should die and go to trash (and fire its Deathknell).
confirmed.observed: After Monster Harpoon resolved, Watchful Sentry remained on the battlefield with meta.__counters.damage=2 but meta.damage=0; trash contained only Monster Harpoon; no death log entry; Sentry's Deathknell did not fire.
confirmed.reason: Damage write/read mismatch. The "damage" effect (effect-executor.ts:407) calls ctx.counters.addCounter(targetId, "damage", amount), which per core operations-impl.ts:459 stores into meta.__counters.damage. The lethal-damage state-based check at state-based-checks.ts:94 reads `const damage = meta?.damage ?? 0` — a different, never-written field — so line 96 `if (damage <= 0) continue` always short-circuits and the kill at lines 109-172 never runs. Result: Watchful Sentry ends up with meta.__counters.damage=2, meta.damage=0, stays on battlefield, no trash move, no Deathknell — exactly as observed. performCleanup is invoked after chain resolution (chain-moves.ts:467/516), so the check does run; it just reads the wrong key.

confirmed.what: 'When you play me' trigger not implemented
confirmed.expected: On play, a triggered ability should go on the chain to heal friendly units here and prompt to move up to one enemy unit from here to its base.
confirmed.observed: Played to base with no chain item, no pendingChoice, no heal/move log entry. Card def (janna-savior.ts) has no abilities[] array — only rulesText.
confirmed.reason: janna-savior.ts:4-18 defines only rulesText with no abilities[] array. Engine reads triggers from card.abilities via getAbilities() (card-lookup.ts:163 returns [] when absent) → toTriggerableAbilities() (trigger-runner.ts:73-76) returns [], so no play-self trigger goes on the chain. Compare gentle-gemdragon.ts:15-34 which correctly implements abilities with trigger:{event:"play-self"}.

confirmed.what: [Reaction] keyword not implemented
confirmed.expected: Janna should be playable at reaction speed and to a battlefield you control.
confirmed.observed: Card def has no keywords/abilities entry for Reaction; only playUnit→base offered (though on turn 1 with no controlled battlefields that specific restriction is expected).
confirmed.reason: Card def at janna-savior.ts:4-18 declares no `keywords` array and no `abilities` entry — [Reaction] appears only in `rulesText`. At runtime the parser (enrich-cards.ts:20-39 → parser/index.ts) does not emit `{type:"keyword", keyword:"Reaction"}` for it; empirically the enriched card has `keywords: undefined` and its sole ability is `{type:"spell", timing:"reaction", ...}`, so `CardDefinitionRegistry.hasKeyword(id, "Reaction")` (card-lookup.ts:118-129) returns false. The `playUnit` move (cards.ts:378-515) only checks `registry.hasKeyword(cardId, "Ambush")` (line 405) for reaction-speed/battlefield targeting and its enumerator only ever offers `location: "base"` gated on active-player/main-phase/neutral-open — there is no Reaction-keyword branch. Result: Janna cannot be played at reaction speed or to a controlled battlefield; only playUnit→base is offered, matching the reported observation. (Note: sfd.json:1987-1990 does carry a Reaction keyword ability, but JSON_SETS in all-cards.ts:828 loads only `venJson`, so sfd.json is not consumed at runtime.)

confirmed.what: Activated ability not offered
confirmed.expected: With the gear ready and 2 mind power available, activateAbility for Temporal Portal (cost [rainbow]+Exhaust) should appear in available moves.
confirmed.observed: Only the legend's activateAbility was listed; Temporal Portal never appeared. Forcing executeMove('activateAbility',{cardId:portal,abilityIndex:0}) did nothing — gear stayed unexhausted, no log entry.
confirmed.reason: Temporal Portal's ability cost is `power: ["rainbow"]` (temporal-portal.ts:13). The activateAbility power-affordability check does a literal per-key lookup `(pool.power[d] ?? 0) < count` at chain-moves.ts:628 (condition) and chain-moves.ts:774 (enumerator). The RunePool.power type is `Partial<Record<"fury"|"calm"|"mind"|"body"|"chaos"|"order", number>>` (types/moves.ts:32,37) — there is no "rainbow" key, so with 2 mind power the lookup yields 0 and `0 < 1` fails affordability. Per rule 135.2.e.5.a, a [rainbow] cost can be paid by Power of any Domain, but neither check sums across domains or special-cases "rainbow". Result: enumerator skips the entry (not offered), and forcing the move hits the condition at :628 which returns false, so the reducer never runs (gear stays unexhausted, no log) — matching both observed symptoms.

confirmed.what: Missing 'choose a friendly unit' target selector
confirmed.expected: rulesText: 'Choose a friendly unit. It deals damage equal to its Might…' — the spell should prompt for one friendly unit whose Might sets the damage amount.
confirmed.observed: Card impl (alpha-strike.ts) encodes amount as {might:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}} with no chooser; there is no target/prompt for the friendly unit selection.
confirmed.reason: alpha-strike.ts:30-32 encodes amount as {might:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"}} with no choose/target step for the friendly unit anywhere in the ability sequence (lines 26-58). The engine's resolveAmount (effect-executor.ts:183-188) only recognizes might:"self"; the object form falls through to `return 0` at line 223, so no prompt is issued and damage is 0. rulesText (line 70) requires "Choose a friendly unit" but the implementation never selects one.

confirmed.what: XP gain over-counts (documented FIXME)
